name: learning
description: Establishing a new skill or mind pattern by experiencing something new.
perceptions: Something happened that could happen again.
I'll remember it for next time.
results: Learning from experience can be a joy, or it can come from the school of hard knocks.
examples: Getting better at a sport just by logging the hours.

guidance.description: The things we learn are not always correct. Sometimes we live in a lopsided environment. Sometimes we're exposed to random stuff. It may be helpful to recognize that sometimes it may help to 'unlearn' errant patterns.

variations.name: learning from a source
variations.description: Establishing new skills or mind patterns by engaging with a school, book, recording, or coach.
perceptions: I want or need to acquire a new skill or pattern.
I'm engaging with someone or something that will help me do this.
results: You may or may not master a subject or skill quickly, but with the right source, you'll be better than before.

comparisons.description: We all learn from experience, becoming better pattern-predictors with every success and failure. When you engage in proactive learning from a reputable source, it will significantly speed your ability to acquire skills and knowledge.

guidance.attribution: The Learning Center at University of North Carolina Chapel Hill

commentaries.quote: Tell me and I forget, teach me and I may remember, involve me and I learn.
For the things we have to learn before we can do them, we learn by doing them.
The beautiful thing about learning is that no one can take it away from you.
Any fool can know. The point is to understand.
Anyone who isn't embarrassed of who they were last year probably isn't learning enough.
The illiterate of the 21st century will not be those who cannot read and write, but those who cannot learn, unlearn, and relearn.
The only thing that interferes with my learning is my education.
